title: Inter-region compacting bridge for tenant-ordered console events
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Console ingests per-tenant usage events from multiple geographic regions. We need one linear, deduplicated, and traceable event stream for downstream billing, SLO alerts, and realtime dashboards. Symptoms include duplicate events when cross-region replication retries, out-of-order event application due to clock skew and transport latency, and inability for downstream consumers to reason about partial aggregates during region failovers.

Proposal: Build a horizontally scalable stream processor — the "inter-region compacting bridge" — that subscribes to region-local ingestion topics (Kafka/Redpanda), performs tenant-keyed windowed compaction, applies deterministic ordering using hybrid logical clocks (HLC) + event-seq, and emits a single global topic per tenant or logical route ("console-metrics.global.<tenant>"). The bridge will: 1) maintain per-tenant state shards with RocksDB-backed storage and incremental snapshots to S3; 2) perform idempotent deduplication via canonical event IDs and lineage hashes; 3) support configurable max-lateness and summary-fallback policies per tenant; 4) enrich events with normalized route ids and sampling tags; 5) emit lineage and trace IDs for debugging and automated replay.

Operational controls: expose control-plane APIs for per-tenant consistency level (strict / eventual / summary), retention of late-event buffers, and on-demand backfill triggers. The processor should support graceful degradation: when a majority of regions are unreachable, it will emit aggregated window summaries rather than raw per-event streams and backfill raw events after recovery.

Out of scope: replacing existing downstream aggregators, heavy ML inference, and changes to client SDKs.

Motivation: Recent incidents (INC-2026-01) exposed 10-20% variance across region-aligned dashboards during replication lag windows, causing false SLA alerts and manual reconciliation. This bridge reduces long-tail divergence, simplifies aggregator logic, and provides clear debugging signals for reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge reads from region-local topics and writes to a single global tenant-scoped topic without introducing duplicates under normal replay scenarios
Deterministic ordering: events with same tenant+route and stable HLC+seq produce identical global ordering across independent replays
Latency: median end-to-end ingest-to-global <= 1.2s and 99th percentile <= 7s under baseline traffic profile
Fault tolerance: when one region is partitioned, bridge emits per-window summaries within SLA and backfills original events into the global topic within the tenant-configured backfill window
Recovery: killing and restarting a bridge instance resumes from the latest durable checkpoint with at-most-once emission of any compacted window
